source-meta.description: Knowledge graph of Frantz Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth (1961). Captures the conceptual structure (colonial Manichaeism, decolonizing violence, national consciousness and its pitfalls, négritude critique, mental disorders as colonial symptom), the figures Fanon engages with (Sartre, Bhabha, Marx, Césaire, the racist colonial-medicine school of Porot/Carothers), and four of the patient case studies from chapter V as reified n-ary events. Extracted from the 2004 Richard Philcox translation by Claude (i2t project) following the InstaGraph schema with the project's two extensions: edges may use `members` for n-ary hyperedges, and edges may carry an explicit `id` matching a node id for reification. Source text: ~/Knowledge/The Wretched Of The Earth.pdf (404 pages, extracted via pdftotext).
source-meta.source: Frantz Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth (1961, Philcox tr. 2004); foreword by Homi K. Bhabha; preface by Jean-Paul Sartre
source-meta.extractor: claude (claude-opus-4-7), schema-compatible with yoheinakajima/instagraph + i2t hyperedge/reification extensions

attrs.label: Frantz Fanon
attrs.role: author of the book; psychiatrist; FLN militant; the philosophical-political voice

attrs.label: Jean-Paul Sartre
attrs.role: wrote the 1961 preface; existentialist interlocutor; endorses Fanon's call for revolutionary violence

attrs.label: Homi K. Bhabha
attrs.role: wrote the 2004 foreword 'Framing Fanon'; postcolonial theorist re-introducing Fanon

attrs.label: Aimé Césaire
attrs.role: Martinican poet; co-founder of negritude; Fanon's teacher

attrs.label: Léopold Sédar Senghor
attrs.role: Senegalese poet/politician; co-founder of negritude

attrs.label: Karl Marx
attrs.role: Fanon stretches Marx for the colonial context — race functions as class infrastructure

attrs.label: V.I. Lenin
attrs.role: theorist of revolution Fanon engages with

attrs.label: Sigmund Freud
attrs.role: Fanon invokes 'Mourning and Melancholia' for case 3 analysis

attrs.label: Simone de Beauvoir
attrs.role: friend; witness to Fanon's last days; quoted in foreword

attrs.label: Steve Biko
attrs.role: South African anti-apartheid; Bhabha invokes him as one heir to Fanon

attrs.label: Charles de Gaulle
attrs.role: French president; quoted speaking of 'yellow multitudes' as colonial vocabulary

attrs.label: François Mauriac
attrs.role: French writer; quoted speaking of 'black, brown, and yellow hordes'

attrs.label: Monsieur Meyer
attrs.role: French Assembly speaker who said the Republic should not be 'defiled' by the Algerian people

attrs.label: Antoine Porot
attrs.role: Algiers School of Psychiatry founder; built the 'doctrine of primitivism' Fanon dismantles

attrs.label: Sutter
attrs.role: Porot's student; co-author of the 1939 paper claiming Algerians are diencephalon-governed

attrs.label: Dr. Carothers
attrs.role: WHO 'international expert' who claimed the normal African is a lobotomized European; 'analyzed' the Mau-Mau revolt as frustration complex

attrs.label: Baruk
attrs.role: psychiatrist whose hysteria report Porot used as platform

attrs.label: Josie Fanon
attrs.role: Fanon's wife; read him reviews of Wretched on his deathbed

attrs.label: The Wretched of the Earth
attrs.role: the book itself; reified — Sartre prefaces it, Bhabha forewords it, the French police seized it on the day Fanon died

attrs.label: Black Skin, White Masks
attrs.role: Fanon's earlier work on the psychic violence of colonial racism in metropolitan France

attrs.label: Sartre's Preface (1961)
attrs.role: the preface that radicalized European reception; reified — Bhabha discusses it

attrs.label: Bhabha's Foreword 'Framing Fanon' (2004)
attrs.role: frame around the Philcox retranslation; reads Fanon for the post-Bandung-collapse era

attrs.label: Mourning and Melancholia
attrs.role: Freud's essay on guilt-after-loss; Fanon invokes it analyzing case 3

attrs.label: The Force of Circumstance
attrs.role: Beauvoir's memoir; quoted by Bhabha for Fanon's 'tuned antennae' remark

attrs.label: Porot's doctrine of primitivism
attrs.role: the racist scientific edifice claiming North Africans are biologically diencephalon-governed; reified — Fanon attacks it as a node

attrs.label: Carothers's 'lobotomized European' claim
attrs.role: WHO-endorsed claim that the normal African resembles a lobotomized European; reified

attrs.label: Decolonization
attrs.role: the central process the book theorizes; described as necessarily violent because colonialism was

attrs.label: Violence (revolutionary)
attrs.role: Fanon's controversial thesis: anticolonial violence is not optional moral excess but the structurally necessary means by which the colonized re-becomes a person

attrs.label: Colonial Manichaeism
attrs.role: the colonial world is divided into two mutually exclusive sectors with no possible mediation

attrs.label: the Compartmentalized World
attrs.role: the spatial form Manichaeism takes — colonist sector vs native sector, with police and army at the boundary

attrs.label: the Colonist's Sector
attrs.role: stone, steel, paved roads, full bellies, white folks; built to last

attrs.label: the Native's Sector
attrs.role: shanty town, Medina, reservation; famished, prostrate, on its knees

attrs.label: National Consciousness
attrs.role: the political-cultural awakening that organizes the struggle; chapter III subjects it to critique

attrs.label: the National Bourgeoisie
attrs.role: the comprador class that inherits colonial structures and reproduces them; the 'pitfall' of national consciousness

attrs.label: the Peasantry
attrs.role: Fanon's revolutionary class — the peasants outside the colonial wage system

attrs.label: the Lumpenproletariat
attrs.role: the displaced rural-to-urban poor; Fanon (against orthodoxy) sees them as revolutionary potential

attrs.label: Spontaneity
attrs.role: the revolt's initial energy; chapter II names both its strength and its weakness when not organized

attrs.label: National Culture
attrs.role: chapter IV: culture rebuilt through and after the liberation struggle, not retrieved as static heritage

attrs.label: Négritude
attrs.role: Césaire/Senghor's affirmative-blackness movement; Fanon is sympathetic but critiques it as continental rather than national, hence trapped in the colonial frame

attrs.label: the Colonized Intellectual
attrs.role: the figure who must journey deep into the people to find legitimate ground

attrs.label: the New Man
attrs.role: the post-colonial human — to be built, not waited on; the conclusion's call

attrs.label: Universal Humanism (false)
attrs.role: the European invocation Fanon rejects; built on Manichaean exclusion in practice

attrs.label: Mental Disorders as Colonial Symptom
attrs.role: chapter V's thesis: psychiatric pathology in colonial subjects is not individual but a social-political wound

attrs.label: Pacification (as euphemism)
attrs.role: the colonial vocabulary's name for ongoing violence; one of 'discipline, tame, subdue, pacify'

attrs.label: Dehumanization
attrs.role: the Manichaean reduction of the colonized to animal — 'zoological terms' in colonial discourse

attrs.label: 'The Last Shall Be the First'
attrs.role: Fanon's borrowed apocalyptic register; Bhabha names the 'religiosity' of his revolutionary wrath

attrs.label: the Third World
attrs.role: the collective political subject Fanon addresses — meant to start a 'new history of man'

attrs.label: Marxist Analysis (stretched for colonial context)
attrs.role: Fanon's amendment: in the colonies, race functions as class — economic infrastructure IS racial superstructure

attrs.label: Front de Libération Nationale (FLN)
attrs.role: Algerian liberation organization; political wing

attrs.label: Armée de Libération Nationale (ALN)
attrs.role: FLN's military wing; treats fighters wounded in combat (case 2's S—— is rescued by ALN soldiers)

attrs.label: the French Army (in Algeria)
attrs.role: occupation force; agent of pacification, torture, and massacre

attrs.label: Colonialism (the system)
attrs.role: the system itself, distinguished from any particular colonial state — the structure being theorized

attrs.label: Colonial Christianity
attrs.role: the Church in the colonies — 'a foreigners' Church'; missionizing as alienation-vector

attrs.label: the Arab League
attrs.role: the supra-national Arab cultural-political body; Fanon contrasts its national heterogeneity with negritude's continental unity

attrs.label: the Négritude Movement
attrs.role: the literary-political movement (Césaire, Senghor, Birago Diop, Hampaté Ba) producing 'black voices'

attrs.label: the Algiers School of Psychiatry
attrs.role: Porot, Sutter, et al.; produced the colonial neuropsychiatric doctrine Fanon dismantles

attrs.label: Algeria
attrs.role: the war's site; Fanon's adopted home

attrs.label: Algiers
attrs.role: the city; site of Porot's school and many of the case studies

attrs.label: the Constantine Region
attrs.role: rural Algeria; site of Case 2's massacred douar

attrs.label: France (metropolitan)
attrs.role: the metropole; the colonist's referenced home

attrs.label: Martinique
attrs.role: Fanon's birthplace; Césaire's home; first site of his analysis of colonial racism

attrs.label: Kenya
attrs.role: site of the Mau-Mau revolt Carothers tried to pathologize

attrs.label: B—— (case I.1)
attrs.role: 26-year-old former taxi driver, FLN militant since age 18; presents with impotence and migraines after wife's rape

attrs.label: B——'s wife
attrs.role: raped by French soldiers during interrogation about her husband's whereabouts; 'a tenacious woman who was prepared to accept anything rather than give up her husband'

attrs.label: B——'s daughter
attrs.role: twenty-month-old at time of incident; B—— develops impulse to tear up her photo

attrs.label: S—— (case I.2)
attrs.role: 37-year-old fellah, Constantine douar; presents with random homicidal impulses after surviving point-blank-range mass execution

attrs.label: the French Officer (case I.2)
attrs.role: arrived by helicopter; declared 'There's too much fuss over this douar; destroy it!'; ordered the massacre

attrs.label: D—— (case I.3)
attrs.role: 19-year-old former student, ALN fighter; presents with depression, hallucinations, and attempted suicide after killing a settler's wife

attrs.label: D——'s mother
attrs.role: killed at point-blank range by a French soldier; D——'s primary attachment

attrs.label: the Settler's Wife (case I.3)
attrs.role: killed by D—— in her home; 'I've got children'; appears in his hallucinations as bloodless, multiplied, demanding her blood back

attrs.label: A—— (case I.4)
attrs.role: 28-year-old European police officer; transferred to anti-FLN brigade; presents with auditory hallucinations of his torture victims' screams

attrs.label: A——'s torture victims (collective)
attrs.role: interrogated, beaten, suspended, near-drowned, electrocuted, in some cases killed at police headquarters

attrs.label: D——'s commander
attrs.role: disarmed D—— after the killing; ordered him to leave; later interrogated him about it

attrs.label: the rape of B——'s wife (case I.1 event)
attrs.role: n-ary reified event; the originating violence; 'It was the rape of a tenacious woman who was prepared to accept anything rather than give up her husband. And that husband was me.'

nodes.label: the rape of B——'s wife (case I.1 event)

attrs.label: the destruction of S——'s douar (case I.2 event)
attrs.role: n-ary reified event; 29 men killed at point-blank range, houses burned, women driven back with rifle butts; S—— wounded in thigh and arm

nodes.label: the destruction of S——'s douar (case I.2 event)

attrs.label: D——'s killing of the settler's wife (case I.3 event)
attrs.role: n-ary reified event; ALN raid on a known-violent settler's estate; the wife alone in the house; D——'s mind on his murdered mother; the kill, the disarming, the interrogation

nodes.label: D——'s killing of the settler's wife (case I.3 event)

attrs.label: A——'s torture sessions (case I.4 event)
attrs.role: n-ary reified event; the police-headquarters interrogation regime — punches, suspension, bathtub, electricity; A—— graduates from amusement to permanent auditory haunting

attrs.label: the Algerian War of Independence (1954-1962)
attrs.role: the encompassing war; the whole book is its theory; n-ary participants include FLN, ALN, French Army, Algerian people, France, settlers

attrs.label: the Bandung Conference (1955)
attrs.role: founding moment of nonalignment; Bhabha names it as the dream now in question

attrs.label: the Sétif Massacre (1945)
attrs.role: French repression of Algerian VE-day demonstration; one of colonial violence's pre-war reference points

attrs.label: Fanon's death (Dec 6, 1961)
attrs.role: leukemia; treated at NIH Bethesda under nom-de-guerre 'Ibrahim Fanon'; French police seized the book in Paris that same day

attrs.label: the Mau-Mau Revolt (Kenya)
attrs.role: Kenyan anti-colonial revolt; Carothers diagnosed it as a 'frustration complex'
